kv.memory.gpg-key-validity-policy: GPG attestor enrollment rule, decided by Mark 2026-09-14 (commit 0edf653): a key is enrollable if its secret half is present (sec field 15 != '#', so smartcard serials count as possession) AND field 2 is not 'r'. EXPIRED keys ('e') are deliberately KEPT -- the operator still holds the secret half, only the declared validity window lapsed, and dropping them deletes a capability rather than labelling it (6 of Mark's 17 keys are expired: f5, hp, blackfedora, NTPsec x2, Nemo). Do not 'fix' expired keys into being rejected. Measured fact: revoking a primary marks every uid 'r', so a revoked key is already refused for having no live uid; the sec-level check is kept anyway because nothing in gpg documents that coupling and this is an authorization decision.
kv.memory.nothing-here-is-published: No crate in this workspace is intended for crates.io -- decided by Mark 2026-09-15, implemented in e0cb678: publish = false on all six. Verified with 'cargo publish --dry-run -p persona-core', which exits 'cannot be published'. Consequences worth keeping: (1) persona-grpc/build.rs reading ../proto, above the package root, is a RECORDED CONSTRAINT not a defect -- cargo package/vendor/docs.rs exclude it, so the crate builds only inside this checkout, and that is fine while the workspace is the only consumer (persona-5s4b.18, undone by 'git mv proto persona-grpc/proto' plus dropping '../'; the whole tree is one file and build.rs is its only reference). (2) description/repository/keywords are deliberately NOT set -- they serve a crates.io listing and a docs.rs page that an unpublishable crate does not have; add them with whichever crate first becomes publishable (persona-5s4b.43). (3) The name 'persona' is TAKEN on crates.io since 2019-10-24 ('Reserving this crate for a Mozilla inside-joke'), so the CLI cannot publish under its current name; persona-core, persona-grpc, persona-attestors and personad were unregistered as of 2026-09-15. Licensing is settled separately and is Mark's call alone: all six declare Apache-2.0, root has LICENSE and LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0. Do not add or change license tags.
kv.memory.persona-core-must-stay-portabl: persona-core is deliberately platform-independent and CI enforces it -- decided by Mark 2026-09-15, implemented in 34c4e4a. A 'portability' job on the existing ubuntu runner runs cargo check --target for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, aarch64-apple-darwin and aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos against persona-core, plus --workspace for darwin; 'make portability' mirrors it and is wired into 'make ci'. Do NOT add --workspace for Windows (persona-grpc is Unix-only by design, 21 UnixListener/UnixStream sites, persona-vvs2) and do NOT propose a windows-latest runner instead: persona-core's tests are byte-exact arithmetic with no platform-dependent behaviour, so running them on Windows proves ~nothing that compiling them does, and drift is the failure worth catching. Measured: adding a std::os::unix MetadataExt to persona-core passes a native cargo check (exit 0) and fails the windows cross-check (exit 101); a type error inside a #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] arm passes a native workspace check (exit 0) and fails the darwin cross-check (exit 101). That second one also retires the local half of the known trap that macOS cfg arms are never type-checked on Linux -- CI's macos-latest leg already caught it, a Linux dev box did not.
kv.memory.personad-may-use-the-network: personad MAY make outbound network connections -- decided by Mark 2026-09-14, after briefly deciding the opposite the same day and reversing it. Reason: did:web is DEFINED as an HTTPS fetch of a DID document, OIDC verification means fetching the issuer's JWKS, and SPIFFE Federation syncs bundles between hosts. Refusing the network does not make those sources local, it makes them unsupported. Do NOT re-propose a no-network posture on the evidence that 'personad connects to nothing today' -- that is true only because the online sources are not built yet, and reading it as intent is the exact mistake that was made and reverted (commits 5edfbb6 then its revert). What still holds: prefer a local daemon that already fetches where one exists (tailscale.rs speaks the LocalAPI over a Unix socket rather than calling the coordination server) -- an efficiency, not a boundary; and a name personad resolves generally comes from local input it does not control, so treat it as untrusted.
kv.memory.platform-docs-describe-the-des: Platform/capability tables in README.md and SPEC-HIA.md describe the DESIGN, with every unbuilt item labelled '(not implemented)' -- decided by Mark 2026-09-15, applied in a84ff14. This extends the settled 'docs list unbuilt COMMANDS and label them' rule to CAPABILITY claims, which promise more than a command name does. Rejected: deleting unbuilt entries (loses the roadmap and would have removed the Windows row entirely) and fixing only the macOS falsehood (leaves Windows Hello, the named-pipe transport and BSD Kerberos still reading as shipped). Ground truth as of 2026-09-15, measured from the code not the docs: PIV is_available() returns false in BOTH cfg arms so it never activates even with --features pkcs11; goa is a placeholder feature with no zbus dep and is target_os=linux; fido2 is real but persona-attestors declares NO default features so it is compiled out unless --features fido2; tailscale hardcodes /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock so it never activates on macOS; did:web, KDE Wallet, WAM, PAM and Kerberos have no implementation at all; personad does not run on Windows. Unconditional sources are OIDC cached and Unix account; everything else has its own runtime check. A real daemon on Mark's Linux box logged five: tailscale, ssh-agent, oidc-cached, gpg, unix.
kv.memory.presence-gate-multi-audience: FetchJWTSVID presence policy is per-audience and reconciled strictest-wins: the gate folds max(require_presence) over EVERY parsed audience, not audience[0]. Chosen over forbidding multi-audience because proto/spiffe/workload/workload.proto:117-118 makes 'repeated string audience' normative ('the audience(s) the workload intends to authenticate against') and the persona_ extension syntax is per-audience by construction (AudienceExtensions::parse is a pure function of one string; there is no control slot or reserved index). max is commutative and PresenceLevel::None is the least element, so no appended audience at any position can lower the bar. Also: the persona_ query-param namespace is CLOSED -- an unimplemented persona_ param is INVALID_ARGUMENT, never ignored. Resolves persona-5s4b.47 and .71.
kv.memory.project-renamed-to-hire: The project is HIRE (Human Identity Runtime Environment), the human counterpart to SPIRE -- renamed from persona by Mark 2026-09-15 in 4f245c8. Repo: github.com/MarkAtwood/project-HIRE. Intent: slot in under SPIFFE/SPIRE as a subproject if they take it; no DNS needed. WHY, so nobody re-proposes 'persona': Persona Identities Inc. (withpersona.com) sells identity verification in the same market, and the shipped systemd unit pointed Documentation= at github.com/persona-id, a stranger's repo, until 930072e -- CNCF donation assigns the trademark to the Linux Foundation, and a mark colliding with a live company in the same industry forces a rename after you have users. Mozilla Persona was a browser identity system besides; crates.io 'persona' taken since 2019. Handles checked 2026-09-15: crates.io 'hire' is TAKEN (case-insensitively, by 'HiRE') and 'hired' is taken -- irrelevant because every crate is publish = false; github.com/hire and github.com/project-hire are taken, github.com/spire-hire is free. NAMES NOW: crates hire-core/hire-attestors/hire-grpc/hire-nmh, binaries 'hired' (daemon) and 'hire' (CLI), unit hired.service, plist hired.plist, spec SPEC-HIRE.md. WIRE FORMAT renamed too: hire_ audience params, the 'hire' JWT claim block, and HKDF SCHEME 'hire-pseudonym-v1:'. TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT RENAMED: (1) the bd prefix stays 'persona-' because ten bead IDs are cited in committed commit messages and bd rename-prefix cannot rewrite git history; (2) signer.rs TEST_MSG stays b'persona ring-removal known-answer vector v1' -- it is the signing input for a known-answer ECDSA vector, sign_raw is deterministic RFC 6979 and openssl's is randomised, so no external oracle can regenerate the signature and recomputing with our own signer would make the test its own oracle.

kv.memory.second-personad-refuses: A second personad REFUSES to start when a live one holds the socket -- decided by Mark 2026-09-15, implemented in 4632471. Detection is an exclusive non-blocking flock on <socket>.lock, taken BEFORE the stale-socket unlink. Chosen because the kernel releases a flock when its holder dies, which is exactly the live-vs-dead question a socket path cannot answer: a crashed daemon's lock is already free so stale-socket cleanup still works unchanged. Rejected: a connect() probe (two daemons starting together both probe, both find nothing, both bind) and documenting the takeover (without a liveness check you cannot even warn, since you never learn you displaced anyone). The NEW instance refuses and exits non-zero with its message on stderr; the running daemon is never touched. The lock is keyed to the SOCKET PATH, not the directory -- the integration tests bind a dozen sockets under /tmp and a directory-wide lock makes them refuse each other. The lock file is never unlinked (removing it races a process that already opened the path). Why it mattered: the two daemons hold different ephemeral signing keys and different pseudonym_ikm, so a takeover silently re-homed every consumer to new pseudonyms and to a JWKS without the kid on its existing token, logging only 'removed stale socket'.
kv.memory.systemd-user-unit-ipaddressden: IPAddressDeny= and IPAddressAllow= do NOTHING in a systemd USER unit. The BPF firewall is not delegated to the per-user manager (user.slice delegates only cpu, memory, pids), so systemd parses the setting, reports no error, and silently does not enforce it. Measured 2026-09-14 on a cgroup v2 host: 'systemd-run --user -p IPAddressDeny=any -- curl https://example.com' returned HTTP 200. RestrictAddressFamilies= DOES work in user units because it is seccomp, applied in-process, needing no delegation: the same test returned 000. personad uses RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX (commit 5edfbb6). Caveat: it filters at socket(2) by family, so it blocks inbound AF_INET too -- there is no seccomp way to allow a loopback listener while refusing outbound. Never recommend IPAddressDeny for a user unit; test any sandbox directive rather than trusting that systemd accepted it.
kv.memory.watch-never-gives-up: persona watch never terminates on its own -- decided by Mark 2026-09-14, implemented in 76a4a7d. When personad is unreachable it logs to stderr and keeps polling; only Ctrl-C ends it, exiting 0. Chosen over 'exit after N consecutive failures' (a threshold nobody can defend, plus a config knob) and over 'exit on first failure' (a routine daemon restart would kill an interactive watch). The reasoning: the fail-open pattern this repo spent 2026-09-14 removing requires a command to TERMINATE before a shell '&&' gate can be fooled, and watch does not terminate, so the exit-non-zero rule that applies to enroll/fetch-x509/trust-bundle/whoami deliberately does NOT apply here. persona whoami is the health check that answers with an exit code. Do not add a failure threshold to watch.
kv.memory.worktree-bisect-poisons-the-sh: Verifying bisectability with 'git worktree add /tmp/X' POISONS the shared cargo target dir, and the symptom looks like a real test regression. Measured 2026-09-15 during the HIRE rename. Mechanism: ~/.cargo/config.toml sets target-dir=/home/mark/Cache/cargo-target for every project, so a worktree at /tmp/pdw5 compiles into the SAME target dir as the real checkout. hire-grpc/tests/e2e.rs bakes concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/tests/verify_jwt_svid.py") in at COMPILE time, so the cached binary carries /tmp/pdw5/... After 'git worktree remove', that path is gone and the test fails with 'python3: can't open file /tmp/pdw5/...'. It failed 3/3 under 'cargo test --workspace' and passed 6/6 under 'cargo test -p hire-grpc --test e2e', which reads exactly like a concurrency flake and is not one. Same trap applies to include_str!, include_bytes! and anything else resolving CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR at compile time. FIX: 'cargo clean -p <pkg>' after worktree-based verification, or set CARGO_TARGET_DIR to a per-worktree path when creating the worktree. DIAGNOSTIC: run the failing test with -- --nocapture; the spawned process prints the dead path. Do NOT go looking for a source-level cause first -- nothing in the repo was wrong.
